questions.question: If 14 January 2022 was Friday, then what will be the day of the week on 28 February 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option(1)

In any two consecutive ordinary years, date of the next year will be one day ahead of the same date of the previous year.

14 January 2022 = Friday

14 January 2023 = Saturday

14 January 2024 = Sunday

If an ordinary year comes immediately after a leap year, then the day on a certain date of the ordinary year will be 2 days ahead of the same date of the leap year upto February

14 January 2025 = Tuesday

From 14 January 2025 to 28 February 2025 = 45 days (42 + 3)

Number of odd days 
= 3 days

Therefore, 28 February = Friday (3 days ahead from Tuesday)

Hence, the correct answer is Option(1)

questions.question:
Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series?

9, 18, 15, ?, 55, 330

If I denotes ‘÷’, J denotes ‘×’, K denotes ‘−’ and L denotes ‘+’, then what will come in place of ‘?’ in the following equation?

(18 I 9) J 12 L 22 K 41 L (36J2) K 2 J 8 = ?
questions.solution:
**BODMAS RULE:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/337cba09b098a129c60c88ca431dc00f7470bb1b39c1452e8d81688a7d6b6b0e.png] 

Given: I → ÷, J → ×, K → −, L → +

Equation: (18 I 9) J 12 L 22 K 41 L (36J2) K 2 J 8 = ?

Interchanging the letters with signs:

= (18 **÷** 9) **×** 12 **+** 22 **−** 41 **+** (36**×**2) **−** 2 **×** 8 

Following the BODMAS rule,

= __2 ____×____ 12__ + 22 − 41 + 72 − __2 ____× 8__

= __24 +____ 22__ − 41 + 72 − 16

= 46 − 41 + 72 − 16

= **61**

Hence, **option 2)** is the correct answer.

questions.question:
Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following set.

(45, 37, 360)

(17, 14, 51)

(NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is NOT allowed)
questions.solution:
The pattern in the given sets is:

** (First term - Second term) × First term = Third term**

We apply the given the pattern on the given sets:

1) **(45, 37, 360)** 

(__**45**____** - 37__**) × 45 = 360 
**__8 × 45__** = 360
360 = 360
LHS = RHS 

2) **(17, 14, 51)** 

(__17____ - 14__) × 17 = 51 
__3 × 17__ = 51
51 = 51
LHS = RHS 

Let's apply the pattern in the given options: 

Option 1) (18, 10, 148) 

(First term - Second term) × First term = Third term

(__18 - 10__) × 18 = 148 

__8 × 18__ = 148

144 ≠ 148 

**LHS ≠ RHS** 

Option 2) (35, 22, 465)
(First term - Second term) × First term = Third term

(__35____ - 22__) × 35 = 465
__13 × 35__ = 465
455 ≠ 465 
LHS ≠ RHS 

Option 3) (21, 17, 87) 
(First term - Second term) × First term = Third term

(__21____ - 17__) × 21 = 87 
__4 × 21__ = 87
84 ≠ 87 
LHS ≠ RHS 

Option 4) (34, 26, 272) 
(First term - Second term) × First term = Third term

(__34____ - 26__) × 34 = 272 
__8 × 34__ = 272
272 = 272 
LHS = RHS 

Option 3 is the only option that is following the pattern.

Hence **the correct answer is option 4)**

questions.question:
Which two numbers, from amongst the given options, should be interchanged to make the given equation correct?

(17 × 4) – (7)² + (63 ÷ 9) × 6 + 83 – 41 = 83
questions.solution:
Given equation:

(17 × 4) – (7)2 + (63 ÷ 9) × 6 + 83 – 41 = 83

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ce560fc547581d91aa28575855976ce48f25a7f9beb85626def585a18220f09c.png] 

We use the hit and trial method with each option:

Option 1) 7 and 9 

__(17 × 4)__ – __(9)____2__ + (__63 ÷ 7__) × 6 + 83 – 41 = 83

68 – 81 + __9 × 6__ + 83 – 41 = 83

__68__ – 81 __+ 54 + 83__ – 41 = 83

__205 - 81 - 41__ = 83

83 = 83 

**LHS = RHS**

Since we got the answer from the first option, we can end the hit and trial method.

Hence **the correct answer is 7 and 9.**
